newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says 1st half primary surplus 2.2 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Peru says 1st half primary surplus 2.2 pct of GDP.

text.p: Peru's Central Reserve Bank President German Suarez said Tuesday the government's first half primary surplus was 2.2 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).

The government has agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on a goal of increasing its primary surplus - the difference between its spending, excluding interest payments on debt, and its income - to one percent of GDP this year from 0.3 percent last year.
Suarez did not give an equivalent figure for the first half surplus in 1995.
He added that the surplus in 1996's first half had enabled the treasury to buy $700 million in foreign currency so far this year on the exchange market.
